summary: Learn GIS, hydraulic modelling, risk mapping, and utility investment planning. Build practical asset-management outputs in five days. Enrol today.
lede: GIS-enabled water and wastewater asset management connects asset location, condition, service criticality, failure likelihood, hydraulic capacity, maintenance history, and financial consequences in one practical operating view. Using the ISO 55000 family as a management-system reference, this course helps you build a structured asset register, validate spatial data, assess risk, and link hydraulic results to operational priorities. You will turn fragmented spreadsheets, drawings, work orders, and model files into repeatable workflows using QGIS or ArcGIS, EPANET, EPA SWMM, and field-data tools such as ArcGIS Field Maps or Survey123. The course produces practical outputs including a GIS-based asset register, risk map, intervention list, investment prioritization matrix, and KPI dashboard structure.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who connect spatial information, network engineering, field activity, and capital planning in water and wastewater utilities or consulting assignments. It suits early to mid-career practitioners with operational exposure who need a common asset management method rather than training in one software product alone.
modules: GIS Asset Registers and Data Quality
prerequisites: You should have practical exposure to water or wastewater utility operations, GIS, network engineering, asset planning, field inspection, or infrastructure finance. Familiarity with spreadsheets and basic spatial data is useful, but advanced hydraulic modelling, programming, and database administration are not required. You do not need to prepare software in advance. The course uses guided examples and supplied datasets, while any use of your own utility data remains subject to internal approvals and data-quality checks.
